header: WHAT THE KOLKATA TAB SHOWS (pure: the catalogue rows and the saved fares are handed in; no request, no database). The tab is the third set of the paid RailRadar month (kolkataSet.ts, kolkataStore.ts): the trains that START at Howrah (HWH), Sealdah (SDAH), Santragachi (SRC) or Kolkata (KOAA) and go over neither Durgapur nor Asansol. The owner added one more rule when he asked for this screen, and I apply it here, to what is saved:
* a train of one of the four must NOT touch any OTHER of the four, whether it stops there or only passes: a Howrah train that goes through Santragachi is not a Howrah train for this tab.

I know what a train touches from two things that are saved: `touches` (the boards of the four stations it is on, halts and pass-throughs alike: RailRadar's boards with includeIntermediate) and its halts. The trains that are left out are kept in a list with the reason (the other station it touches), so that the owner can see what the rule removed, and nothing is hidden without being counted. The times are the times AT THE STARTING STATION, and the days are the days it leaves there (the train starts here, so nothing is moved on by a day). Nothing is guessed: a train whose first halt has no readable departure is not drawn, and a train with no fare says why (the reservation system does not sell it, or it sold none, or it was not collected).

behaviours: the four stations are Howrah, Sealdah, Santragachi and Kolkata, in the owner's order, and are the same codes the harvest uses
only the four codes are a station (anything else, a number, nothing, is not)
a train touches another of the four when its board list or its halts say so: Santragachi on the boards (13023, and 12839 which only PASSES it), Kolkata among the halts (12000)
a train that touches no other is its own station's alone (12347 at Howrah: touches only HWH, halts at HWH and BWN)
its own station is never 'another': a Howrah train that stops at Howrah again is not out for that
Howrah shows 12347, 12021, the local 37101 and the special 03003; 13023, 12839 and 12000 are left out, each once
each train left out says which other station it touches
a train that is out of the set (it goes over Durgapur) is neither shown nor in the left-out list
a train belongs to its STARTING station only: Sealdah's list has no Howrah train, and no train is in two stations' lists
a row is a train of the tab only when its first halt is its own starting station
a train's time is its departure at its starting station, it has no arrival there, and its days are the days it leaves (no day is moved on)
a train that runs on some days keeps them in the week's order
the kind: Suburban, EMU, MEMU and Passenger are local; 'Train on Demand' is special; the rest are express
a train with no readable departure, or with no readable day, is not drawn, and is counted as unreadable (never given a made-up time)
the trains are in the order of the clock at the station, and the same minute by train number
the fare state: saved (classes answered), none (the service sold nothing), not-collected (sold, but no row), not-sold (the reservation system does not sell it)
the answer for Howrah has its express (12347, 12021, 03003) and local (37101) trains apart, in the clock's order
it carries the counts of all FOUR stations, so the picker shows them whichever one is open
the date of the OLDEST record shown, the date of the OLDEST fare shown (12021's, 27 Nov), and the number with a fare
a station with no fare at all has no fare date
the answer passes the check that guards what is drawn; a damaged one does not
a run time is said in hours and minutes, and not at all when it is not known
